notes: v11's design with every curve end given a source (docs/plan-evolving-score.md section 4, EV4; the user's decision of 2026-10-03, section 9 Q2, A). Each end is one of four kinds, named in its component's `sources`: DOMAIN, the limit the quantity cannot pass; GATE, the gate on the same measurement, so the zero end sits where the gate already says not a game; MEANING, a one-sentence reading of the quantity; REFERENCE, a quantile of the 20 published band games (the 21 agreed on 2026-09-28 less intransitive), the k-th lowest or highest at k = ceil(0.1 n), read ONCE from the library under v11 on 2026-10-03 and pinned here as a number. The band no longer places the scale: `anchor` lost --write and reports where the band sits against these ends, and `calibrate` checks the scale. Every weight, family, curve kind, gate and llm_weight is v11's to the digit, so a v11-to-v12 move of any score is the scale changing source and nothing else. The ends, the read and its amendment A1 (skill_gradient's 0.99 ladder rule applied per run, because the first rule left 8 of 20 games and stopped), the predictions and their grading are in docs/reference/v12-calibration.md, pre-registered before any table was computed. `evidence` and `roster_rho` are v11's: the components and their noise did not change.

gates.reason: a searching player must beat a random one, or there is nothing to play
a game that mostly fails to finish is not a game, and a half of the ladder that mostly fails to finish is not rescued by the other half finishing
with no choices there is no play
a game that competent players almost always draw is not a contest, and averaging in the games their weaker opponents lost outright does not make it one
a game decided before either player has developed anything is not a game; pooled with a shuffle at the other end of the ladder the mean describes no game that was played
doubling the thinking budget must be worth at least a few Elo, or skill does not exist here

a game where half of all contests are over in a handful of moves is decided by an opening trap, not by play; read on the half of the ladder that falls into the trap, because every quick kill in a run is a weak-half game and the strong half is only the denominator
